title: Spirometry for children
what: Your child blows into a tube, and a device shows how well their lungs work. Often there is a game on the screen to help.
why: For a frequent cough, wheezing, suspected asthma, and to check how well treatment is working.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes; the result is given right away
tell_doctor: Which inhalers and medicines your child uses
If your child has a cold or fever now
If your child is afraid of procedures

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Sometimes inhalers are not given for a few hours before the test. Only the doctor can tell you. Do not stop them on your own.

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: If your child is sick, it is usually better to move the test. Call the clinic.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: A light breakfast, not a big one. It is hard to blow with a full stomach.

prepare.title: Talk about it
prepare.text: At home, explain that they will need to blow hard, like blowing out birthday candles.

steps: Your child sits up straight, and a soft clip is put on the nose
They are shown what to do, often with a game on the screen
They take a deep breath and blow hard into the tube
It is repeated a few times to get a good result
Sometimes they get an inhaler, and the test is repeated after 15 to 20 minutes
feel: The nose clip feels a bit strange
Blowing many times can make them dizzy or cough
after: The result is usually given right away
The doctor will explain it and change the treatment if needed
Praise your child. It helps next time
red_flags: After the test, your child has trouble breathing or is wheezing, and the inhaler does not help: call emergency services

faq.q: From what age can it be done?
faq.a: Usually from age 5 or 6, when a child can follow instructions. Ask your doctor.

faq.q: What if it does not work?
faq.a: That happens. The test is repeated, sometimes on another day.

reminders.text: Your child's spirometry is tomorrow. Do not give the inhaler if the doctor said so. Bring a toy.
